chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Maymoun, who said:

Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) arrived performing Tamattu' on the night of Arafah, so he circumambulated, and freed from Ihram, and went to one of his slave girls. Then he began with the Hajj and went out.

key_terms.أَهَلَّ بِالْحَجِّ: He began with the Hajj (entered Ihram for Hajj)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعاً: Performing Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately with a break in Ihram)
key_terms.وَأَحَلَّ: And he freed from Ihram (exited the state of consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual procedure of Hajj al-Tamattu' as demonstrated by the Imam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical application of Hajj al-Tamattu' by Imam al-Hassan (peace be upon him), specifically illustrating the flexibility in timing the transition from Umrah to Hajj. It serves as a key evidence for scholars regarding the validity of performing the Ihram for Hajj on the night of Arafah, thereby clarifying the temporal boundaries of the 'Tamattu' state.
